title: Commutative extensions of groups of multiplicative type are of multiplicative type
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. All group schemes are affine $F$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. A group scheme is of multiplicative type if it is isomorphic to $D(M)=\operatorname{Spec}F[M]$ for a finitely generated abelian group $M$, with comultiplication $e_m\mapsto e_m\otimes e_m$ on the group-algebra basis. Let $q:E\to Q$ be a homomorphism whose coordinate-ring map is faithfully flat, meaning that extension of scalars is exact and detects zero modules, and let $N=\ker q$ be its scheme-theoretic kernel. Assume $N$ and $Q$ are of multiplicative type. If $E$ is commutative, then $E$ is of multiplicative type. No smoothness or connectedness assumption is made on $E,N,Q$.

source.place: Corollary 12.22, printed p.239; the sufficient direction, with an explicitly specified faithfully flat quotient.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-multiplicative-additive-vanishing-criterion] to $N$ and $Q$. Each is affine of finite type by the hypotheses, and its given multiplicative-type presentation is exactly the diagonalizable presentation in that criterion. Consequently every homomorphism $N\to\mathbf G_{a,F}$ and every homomorphism $Q\to\mathbf G_{a,F}$ is zero. This assertion concerns scheme morphisms, hence all algebra-valued points, including nilpotent test algebras.

source.place: Corollary 12.22, printed p.239, proof; Theorem 12.18(a),(b),(d), printed pp.237–238.

proof.text: Let $u:E\to\mathbf G_{a,F}$ be any group-scheme homomorphism. Its restriction $u|_N$ is zero by step 1. Apply [lem-sfb-faithfully-flat-group-quotient-universal] to $G=E$, the given $q:E\to Q$, and $H=\mathbf G_{a,F}$; the additive group is affine of finite type by [def-sc-gm-ga]. The stipulated faithful flatness of the coordinate map is exactly the hypothesis of that lemma. It gives a homomorphism $v:Q\to\mathbf G_{a,F}$ with $u=v\circ q$. Step 1 gives $v=0$, so $u=0$. Thus every homomorphism $E\to\mathbf G_{a,F}$ vanishes.

source.place: Corollary 12.22, p.239, exactness of the displayed Hom sequence; Theorem 5.13, p.101.

proof.text: The group $E$ is affine of finite type and commutative by assumption, and step 2 proves the remaining hypothesis of [lem-sfb-multiplicative-additive-vanishing-criterion]. Its converse therefore supplies a finitely generated abelian group $M$ and an isomorphism $E\simeq D_F(M)$. This is the required multiplicative-type conclusion. The criterion and quotient lemma require neither smoothness nor connectedness, so the argument also covers infinitesimal kernels.
